Sect: Independent

Legend holds that the Baali descend from a Third Generation vampire who dallied with a slave-boy and turned against his own siblings, striking foul pacts with powers beyond the world and gathering followers who made war on the Second City before being routed and destroyed - or so it was believed. Long thought exterminated by the Inquisition, the Baali have resurfaced in modern nights, and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} alike set aside their rivalry to burn out any nest they find. Rather than cackling devil-worshippers, most Baali are patient sages and academics who genuinely pursue forbidden knowledge, seducing the faithless with a genteel offer of enlightenment rather than crude displays of evil. Their havens can be recognized by strange sigils, places of power, and deformities among nearby livestock and children. As they age, Baali fall further from their human roots, and older members often keep vermin as pets or companions in vast, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}-rivaling hordes.

Disciplines: Daimoinon, Obfuscate, Presence

Advantage: Baali command the infernal Discipline of Daimoinon and can sense places and souls tainted by corruption.

Disadvantage: True Faith and holy relics inflict double damage on the Baali, and when confronting a mortal with True Faith they must risk twice the normal number of Traits to avoid recoiling or frenzy.

Organization: Never numerous, the Baali's ranks have thinned further as their unity fractures and enemies close in from every side. They operate as isolated cells or lone missionaries of forbidden lore rather than a unified clan, evangelizing quietly for the glory of Those-Who-Wait.
